content:
Has anyone worked on dg-categories in Lean and does anyone feel strongly about how they should enter mathlib? I understand that there is some interest in A-infinity categories (#new members > A-Infinity Categories), which I suppose is a generalization, but I think a standard definition of dg-categories is probably what should enter mathlib?

I don't know much about A-infinity categories but I am interested in working on dg-categories, so I'd like to hear opinions.

I posted a code snippet giving a definition a while ago: #general > O(1000) definitions for Annals @ 💬
I do not claim that’s the best way of doing things.
When you say you intend to "work on dg-categories", do you have specific statements in mind?
Some things I want to define are the homotopy category, quasi-equivalence, and pretriangulated dg-categories
I saw your definition and I've actually been using it, though with cochain complexes instead
Ah, yes, I had written it in a hurry without thinking about the homological/cohomological conventions. I agree it’s more reasonable with cochain complexes.

I suppose that the process of having a piece of widely used math "enter mathlib" entails exactly a discussion of what is the "standard definition." From our perspective working on A∞ categories (you linked above), it seems perfectly reasonable to define a dg category as an A∞ category with higher mu's trivial, and show equivalence to the quick EnrichedCategory definition.

Jack McKoen said:

Some things I want to define are the homotopy category, quasi-equivalence, and pretriangulated dg-categories

In particular, we will want to eventually define (the appropriate generalizations of) these notions also for A∞ categories, which further motivates the most-general and most-modular approach that mathlib usually takes.

Justin Mu has started a first PR #40984, and we will resubmit an improved version soon. See the discussion here on Zulip (#PR reviews > Towards A∞ categories (#40984)) as well as on GitHub for some technical details, where we are trying to figure out together what will be most usable.
Also are you aware of Joël Riou's paper https://afm.episciences.org/15978 ?

Disclaimer: I don’t know a lot about A∞-categories, but I am skeptical of the idea of taking "A∞-categories with higher mu's trivial" as the definition of a dg-category: I am worried that this would make things unnecessarily complicated for users who don’t care at all about A∞-categories. Showing equivalence with the EnrichedCategory definition seems like a heavy statement lean-wise (not necessarily hard, but comprising many defs before it can be satisfying). If one wants to formalize something that is more easily done from the EnrichedCategory definition (or simply written in that language in the literature), constant translation through such equivalence might be a pain to deal with.

A nice long term goal for dg-categories in mathlib would be to define their model category structure.
I fully agree with @Robin Carlier's message above.

Marco David said:

Also are you aware of Joël Riou's paper https://afm.episciences.org/15978 ?

I am aware of it but what in particular do you think I should take into account?

Marco David said:

I suppose that the process of having a piece of widely used math "enter mathlib" entails exactly a discussion of what is the "standard definition."

Surely the standard definition is the enriched approach? At least, the all the literature I have seen (though I have not seen much) defines dg-categories in this way. Is it common to define a dg-category as a specialization of an A∞ category? This seems like something to be recovered later, and as Robin says, I will mostly want to formalize things from the literature that are written from the enriched perspective

The working definition in question:

abbrev DGCategory (R : Type w) [CommRing R] :=
  EnrichedCategory (CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{w} R) ℤ)
